Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2199 of 2011 
with 
Civil Petition Nos. 1671-1672 and 2198 of 2011.
lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Petitioner (in CP No. 2199 of 2011) 
Fida M Kamal, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Petitioner (in CP No. 1671 of 2011) 
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate instruct by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Petitioner (in CP No. 1672 of 2011) 
AF Hasan Ariff J, Senior Advocate instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner (in CP No. 2198 of 2011) 
Md Khalilur Rahman, Advocate instructed by Md Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Respondents (in CP Nos. 2199 &1671-72 of 2011) 
None represented ----- For the Respondents (in CP No.2198 of 2011)
parties:
Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza ------ Petitioner. (In CP No. 2199 of 2011)
Vs.
Anwarul Hasan and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
23. Mr AF Hassan Ariff appearing in CP No.2198 of 2011 separately argued that plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza proved conclusively that he was the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the actual owner of the suit plot and, as such, he had every right to dispose of his property by way of sale and since RAJUK did not give permission to sell the same in spite of prayer made by him, he had no other alternative but to file the suit. But the High Court Division, on an erroneous approach to the case and also on misreading of the evidence on record, found that the plaintiff was not the real owner of the suit plot and thus dismissed the suit. He has further submitted that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division erred in law in holding that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar was the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the owner of the suit plot ignoring the fact that the plaintiff Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Title Suit No.176 of 2004 produced all the relevant original documents from his custody, such as: letter of allotment, money receipts showing payment of installments in respect of the suit plot, paper handing over possession of the suit plot to him, the standard lease deed, approved plan dated 29-10-1966 by the then DIT for constructing building on the suit plot, permission letter issued by DIT to undertake construction on the suit plot, DCR, mutation khatian, rent receipts and RS Khatian prepared in his name. He has lastly submitted that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division rejected the plaintiff's claim that he was the Executive Engineer of C&B under the Ministry of Communications considering the extraneous matters than the documentary evidence produced by him and thus fell into an error in dismissing the suit. 

 24. Mr Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate, entering caveat on behalf of the respondents in CP Nos.2199 of 2011, 1671 and 1672 of 2011, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment passed by the learned Judges of the High Court Division affirming those of the trial Court passed in the respective suit. He has submitted that in view of the conflicting pleadings of the respective party, possession of the suit plot was a very vital and crucial issue to be decided in the suits. The trial Court as well as the High Court Division considering the tenancy agreements entered into by late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar with the tenants, rent receipts, RS Khatian, bills of the utility services, came to the specific finding that the plaintiffs father, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar had been in possession of the suit plot right from the time of delivery of possession, pursuant to the letter of allotment and rightly decreed Title Suit No.81 of 2006 and dismissed the other two suits. He has further submitted that the findings of the Courts below that plaintiffs' (Title Suit No.81 of 2006) father, late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar was the actual allottee of the suit plot and he never entered into any contract with defendant No.1, MA Hashem or defendant No.4, MNH Bulu and that defendant No.2, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur was a fake person, are concurrent findings of facts based on proper consideration of the evidence on record adduced by the parties, there is no scope of interference by this Court with such findings and, as such, the question of sending the suit or the appeal back on remand to the Court below does not arise at all and he submits that all the petitions be dismissed. 

 The trial Court dismissed the suit on the findings, inter alia, that plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, was not the original allottee, therefore, RAJUK could not give permission to him to sell the suit plot and that RAJUK recognized Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar as the allottee of the suit plot and also approved Eastern Housing Limited as his attorney; the plaintiff's suit was not maintainable. In coming to the said findings, the trial Court held that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who was the Executive Engineer of C&B and that RS khatian No.1174 in respect of the suit plot was recorded in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar; plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as PW 1 in his cross-examination clearly stated that he never resided at 157, Bara Moghbazar and while he deposed, he was residing at 911/1 Shewrapara as a tenant of one Monowara; the suit plot was allotted to Executive Engineer, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and admittedly the plaintiff was Diploma Engineer and therefore, it was not believable that he could join a big Department like C&B as Assistant Engineer in 1950/1952 and was promoted as the Executive Engineer in 1956/57 and therefore, it could not be accepted that the plaintiff got the allotment of the suit plot as Executive Engineer. The trial Court further noticed that PW 1 (Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza) admitted in his cross- examination that in 1965, he was a voter at Ishwardi and after liberation of Bangladesh, he participated in an election at Fulbaria under the district of Dinajpur, which was not believable, asit was not natural that a person, who served as an Executive Engineer, would go to an Upazila and participate in the election. The trial Court further observed that it was not natural that a person, who became the Executive Engineer, would live at Pabna, then at Dinajpur and then in Dhaka. The trial Court further observed that it was also not believable that a person, who got a plot from RAJUK at Gulshan, would reside at Ishwardi in the district of Pabna and then at Fulbaria in the district of Dinajpur. Although the plaintiff claimed that he accepted domicile certificate but that was not with him. The trial Court further observed that the plaintiff in his cross-examination admitted that though he served as an Executive Engineer in C&B, he did not open any bank account, which also proved that he was not an Executive Engineer, because the salary of a first class employee is given through cheque and in the absence of bank account, he could not draw his salary. The trial Court further noticed that the plaintiff admitted in his cross-examination that he had gone to India in 1958 and married his cousin (খালাতো বোন) at 'Arai' in India. The trial Court noticed that a person, who migrated to this country, in 1947 and was a high official in C&B, could not go to India without the permission of his office or the Government for marrying there. PW2, a guard of Sonali Bank, Motijheel Branch, was disbelieved by the trial Court on the ground that when the plaintiff admitted that he had no bank account, it was not believable that he would be acquainted with a guard of Sonali Bank. The trial Court also observed that it was not natural that the plaintiff, who claimed to be an Executive Engineer, would develop a relationship with a guard of a bank. The trial Court disbelieved PW 3 on the ground that he deposed that he got himself acquainted with the plaintiff through one of the relative, namely, Shamim; when PWI in his cross-examination admitted that he had no relative in this country. (PWs 2 and 3 were examined to prove plaintiff's possession in the suit plot.) The trial Court relied on the evidence of DW1, an official of RAJUK that no application was filed by the plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, to RAJUK for permission to sell the suit plot to MNH Bulu and that no application was filed by the plaintiff to RAJUK on 18-2-2004 to sell the suit plot. The trial Court further held that RAJUK did not recognize the plaintiff of the instant suit as the allottee of the suit plot, rather RAJUK admitted Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar as the allottee and approved the power of attorney given by him to Eastern Housing Limited. 

 35. The learned presiding Judge noticed that on 18-9-2008, i.e. long after 4 years and 4 months of the institution of the suit (the suit was instituted on 26-5-2004) further amendment was made in paragraph 4 of the plaint as to the number of the deed of lease executed and registered by RAJUK, i.e. figure "1198" was replaced by the figure "7198". The learned Judge came to the finding that the plaintiff did not produce any copy of his application filed to RAJUK for sale permission of the suit plot. The learned Judge further noticed that RAJUK in its written statement stated that "such file in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as mentioned is not traceable in the office of RAJUK and I find plaintiff did not produce any copy of his application in the suit or exhibited it." The learned Judge concluded that "So, it may be legally presumed that such application was not filed and alternatively it may be presumed that the suit plot was not allotted to the plaintiff." Considering the deposition of PW1, the learned Judge observed that after his son disappeared with his brother-in-law in 1972 who had allegedly gone to the suit plot in the month of December, 1972, till filing the suit on 26-5-2004, i. e. for the last 32 years, the plaintiff did not go to the suit plot and that he did not also take any step through legal process for recovery of the same and that had he been allotted the suit plot as lessee by RAJUK, he ought to have informed this fact to RAJUK for recovery of possession, but he did nothing. Although, in his deposition, the plaintiff claimed that he had lived in the suit plot till 1971 and then left the suit plot for security reason keeping his Caretaker, Abul Khair and then again came back there, in 1972, he did not examine Abul Khair. The plaintiff did not also produce his domicile certificate. The learned Judge further noticed that the plaintiff stated in his deposition that after coming to Dhaka, he resided at 154, Bara Moghbazar thereafter at Mirpur with his uncle, but the RS Khatian was prepared. in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar and not in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 154, Bara Moghbazar. The learned Judge further observed that if it was true that after getting permission for construction from RAJUK, the plaintiff constructed a two storied building on the suit plot then a man of prudence could not sit idol and keep mum when he found his property occupied by a third person and dismantling the building standing therein. The learned Judge came to the finding that the claim of possession of the plaintiff in the suit plot was not true. The plaintiff claimed to be a Government employee, but he had no bank account, then how he could draw his salary, because salary could not be paid in hand or in cash but through a bank account. The learned Judge' further noticed that the plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza first produced "allotment deed as deed No.1198 and no sooner its genuinity when challenged he produce (sic) deed No.7198 shows how quick such forgery could (sic) made. Both the deeds are on record." 

 38. The learned presiding Judge observed that though defendant No.3 (also plaintiff in Title Suit No.176 of 2004) claimed that he was in possession in the suit plot, but "no where he ever stated how he was inducted into possession and when he was dispossessed." There was only a solitary statement in his deposition that in 1970, (it will be 1972) he sent his brother-in-law and the only son to the suit plot and thereafter, both of them disappeared. If that fact was true, then the defendant and other family members would have left no stone unturned to find out the whereabouts of his only son and brother-in-law, but nothing was done. PW 1 stated that he made a GD entry, but the copy of GD entry was not produced. The learned Judge observed that since the time of missing of his only son and the brother-in-law till the date of hearing of the appeal, the defendant did not take any step either to recovery the possession of the suit plot or for a declaration that he was the lawful owner thereof. Considering the documents of the plaintiffs, namely: allotment letter (exhibit-1); general power of attorney executed by the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibits-2, 3, and 3Ka) in favour of Eastern Housing Limited; matriculation certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibit-4); intermediate certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Bara Moghbazar (exhibit-4Ka); BSc Engineering certificate Part II of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibit-4Kha); BSc Engineering certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibit- 4Ga); Pakistani domicile declaration of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (exhibit-5); deed of sale executed in favour of AZM Sanaullah dated 24-9- 1957 (exhibit-6); deed of sale executed by AZM Sanaullah dated 24-9-1957 in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in respect of the property at Bara Moghbazar; deed of heba dated 17-8-1979 executed by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in favour of his wife, Selima Begum (exhibit-7); approved plan of DIT (exhibit-8); voter identity card of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (exhibit- 9); passport of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (exhibit-'9Ka); certificate issued by the Government of Canada in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (exhibit-10); promotion letters (exhibit-11 series); allotment letter of DIT in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (exhibit-12); receipts showing payment of installments (exhibits-12Ka to 12Gha); the letters written by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar to DIT informing about the fact of payment of installments (exhibits 13 uma to 13Cha); letter written by the then DIT to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as to the delivery of possession of the suit plot and also asking him to deposit Taka 51 (exhibit-14); Standard lease deed of the suit plot (exhibit-15); letter of DIT approving plan (exhibit-16); photostat copy of approved plan of DIT (exhibit-16Ka); letter of House Building Finance Corporation sanctioning loan (exhibit-17); mortgaged deed executed by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar in favour of House Building Finance Corporation (exhibit-17Ka); tenancy agreements between Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the tenants spreading over the period from 1967 to 2000 (exhibit-18 series); letters of WASA for water connection and bills showing payment of gas, electricity and WASA charges (exhibits-19 series); municipal assessment tax for the period 1967 to 1968 (exhibit-20); the receipts of tax as to the payment of tax of the Municipality for the period 2003 to 2004 (exhibit-20Kha); receipt showing payment ofland tax (exhibits-21-21 Na); RS Khatian No. 1174 recorded in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibit-22); Memorandum and Articles of Association of Bengal Development Corporation Limited (exhibits-23-23Ka); audit reports of Uttara Bank Limited for the period 1996-2001 (exhibits-24-24Uma); letter of DIT to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar regarding fees for changing the suit plot from residential to commercial (exhibit-25); letter issued by RAJUK to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar approving the conversion of the suit plot into a commercial plot from residential plot (exhibit-26); certified copy of the general power of attorney executed by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar in favour of Eastern Housing Limited (exhibit-27); approval letter of RAJUK in respect of the power of attorney given by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza to Eastern Housing Limited (exhibit-28); approved plan (exhibits 29-29Kha); notices published in the Daily Janakatha (exhibits-30-30Kha); corrigendum published in the Daily Janakatha (exhibits 31-31Ka); Death certificate of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibit 32); news published in different news papers by Uttara Bank Limited on the death of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (exhibit-33); Succession certificate issued by the ward Commissioner of Ward No.53, Dhaka City Corporation (exhibit-33Ka); Succession certificate issued by the 3'd Joint District Judge, Dhaka (exhibit-34); plaint of Title Suit No.51 of 2004 (exhibit-35); plaint of Title Suit No.176 of 2004(exhibit-36); pay bills (exhibits-37-37Ka); Passport No.B-57985 of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar (exhibit-38); came to the positive finding that the plaintiffs proved that from 1967 till the hearing of the suit, i.e. for more than 35 years, they had been in possession of the suit plot and such continuous possession gave them title and that the lessor, RAJUK always recognized the plaintiffs as the lessees and it did not challenge their title in the suit plot in any form. The learned Judge further held that the case of defendant No.3, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, could be considered if he were found to be in possession "but his case on possession is down right false" and by his own statement, it was proved that at no point of time, he was in possession thereof. Considering the documents filed by defendant No.3, namely: letter of allotment dated 21-3-1962, receipts showing deposit of installments against the suit plot, letter as to the delivery of possession of the suit plot, approved plan by RAJUK for construction on the suit plot and the certified copy of the RS Khatian (these documents were proved and marked as exhibits 1,2 series, 3, 6 and 9 respectively) further held that "the exhibits although resemble or appear to be true are not genuine or true, but he has manage(sic) to get those document which apparently original documents" to claim title to the suit plot. If the case of defendant No.3 that he was thrown out of his possession of the suit plot after he was inducted therein and that too when his only son with his brother-in-law disappeared in 1972, was true, he would have left no stone unturned to get back his son and brother-in-law and also the possession of the suit plot, but he only made a GD entry and moved the Parliamentary Standing Committee which had no business in the matter "of declaring title and getting possession of a property which can only be done by Court." Another aspect is that defendant No.3 gave his address "in his suit as of the disputed allotted suit plot which shows that he is a fake person as addressless person can be used by any person for any illegal purpose." The learned Judge further observed that it was the case of defendant No.3 that he entered into an agreement with MNH Bulu to sell the suit plot and to prove that fact defendant No.3 could examine Bhulu but he did not which shows that he lives in false in making out his case." The learned Judge found the documents of the plaintiffs genuine considering two vital and relevant facts (i) when on physical verification of the suit plot, a fraction chhatak/decimal was found to be in excess of the allotted plot, the then DIT directed their father (wrongly written as plaintiff) to pay for the excess land and by the 5th deposit excess amount of Taka 51 was paid and (ii) plaintiffs' predecessor, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar took loan from House Building Finance Corporation by mortgaging the suit plot as evidenced by exhibit-17. Defendant No.3 did not produce any paper to show that he was present when the suit property/plot was measured and in fact, he was never inducted into possession of the suit plot. 

 49. Title Suit No.l76 of 2004, giving rise to Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2198 of 2011, was filed by one Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza impleading the officials of RAJUK only for two reliefs (i) that he was legally entitled to get the sale permission of the suit plot and the defendants were bound to issue such sale permission on receiving the proper transfer fees from him and (ii) that the defendants were bound to dispose of the application filed by him on 18-2-2004 for sale permission of the suit plot within a specified time as to be directed by the Court claiming himself to be the allottee of the suit plot. He claimed that he was an Executive Engineer of C&B under the Ministry of Communications. But in support of his said claim, he did not file a single paper. The trial Court considering the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, dismissed the suit on the clear findings, inter alia, that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who was the Executive Engineer of C&B ; the plaintiff was a Diploma Engineer and it was not believable that he could join a big department like C&B as an Assistant Engineer in 1950/1952 and then promoted as Executive Engineer in 1956/57 The trial Court further observed that the plaintiff in his cross-examination admitted that though he served as an Executive Engineer in C&B, he did not open any  bank account, which also proved that he was not an Executive Engineer, because the salary of a first class employee is given through cheque and in the  absence of bank account* he could not draw his  salary and that he was not the allottee of the suit allot. Therefore, RAJUK could not give permission to him to sell the suit plot. RAJUK recognized Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar as the allottee of the suit plot and also approved Eastern Housing Limited as his attorney and that the suit was not maintainable. The trial Court further held that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who was an Executive Engineer of C&B and RAJUK did not recognize the plaintiff as the allottee of the suit plot. RS Khatian  No.11174 in respect of the suit plot was recorded  in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar and plaintiff Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as PW1 in his cross-examination  clearly stated that he never resided at 157, Bara  Moghbazar and while he deposed, he was residing at 911/1 Shewrapara as a tenant of one Monowara. The trial Court further held that no application was filed to RAJUK by the plaintiff on 18-2-2004 for permission to sell the suit plot to MNH Bulu. While dismissing the first appeal, the learned Judges affirmed the said findings of the trial Court, but giving their own reasonings. The learned Judges gave further finding that the plaintiff did not produce any copy of his application filed to RAJUK for sale permission of the suit plot. The learned Judges taking into notice of the fact that RAJUK in its written statement stated that "such file in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as mentioned is not traceable in the office of RAJUK" concluded that "so, it may be legally presumed that such application was notified and alternatively it may be presumed that the suit plot was not allotted to the plaintiff." The learned Judges came to further finding that documents filed by the plaintiff exhibited in the suit clearly show that those were prepared in the name  of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar which was admittedly the permanent address of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun  Reza, a different person. The learned Judges further held that the suit of the plaintiff for sale permission simpliciter was not maintainable as he himself admitted in the plaint as well as in his deposition that he was out of possession and that Title Suit No.81 of 2006 filed by the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar for declaration of title and permanent injunction heard simultaneously by the same Court (the plaintiff was defendant No.3 in the suit) was decreed. The learned Judges came to further finding that though PW I (Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza) claimed that he was an Executive  Engineer, but his testimony regarding Service  Book, ACR, and Organogram clearly proved that he was not a service holder at all. The findings given by the trial Court as well as the High Court Division as to the actual allottee of the suit plot are so specific and well reasoned that we see no scope of touching with those findings. More interesting thing is that the whole case of the plaintiff was that he filed an application to RAJUK on 18-2-2004 to give him permission to sell the suit plot to MNH Bulu, but that application was not disposed of by RAJUK, which gave him the cause of action to file the suit. And, in fact, the plaintiff prayed for a relief to give direction to RAJUK to dispose of his said application within certain specific time fixed by the Court, but no such application was filed before the Court. Thus, the very foundation of the plaintiff's case had no existence. So, the plaintiff was not entitled to get any relief in the suit. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan and Mr AF Hasan Ariff, appearing for the petitioner, could not lay their hands on any of the material evidence on record to assail the findings jotted down hereinabove either on the ground of misreading or non-consideration of any material evidence by the Courts below and thus, term those as perverse. (The reasonings, given by the trial Court and the learned Judges of the High Court Division in coming to their findings have been exhaustively noted while summarizing their findings, so those are not repeated.) 

 52. In the suit, plaintiff of Title Suit No.51 of 2004, MA Hashem and Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, plaintiff of Title Suit No.176 of 2004, were impleaded as defendant Nos.1and 3 respectively and Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur was impleaded as defendant No.2. The trial Court decreed the suit on the clear findings that the plaintiffs proved conclusively that the suit plot was allotted to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Bara Moghbazar their father and he constructed building therein on obtaining loan by mortgaging the same with House Building Finance Corporation and had been in possession thereof by letting out the same to various tenants as apparent vide exhibit-18 series. Defendant No.3. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was not the owner of the suit plot. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence of MA Hashem examined in Title Suit NO.51 of2004 further held that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur neither was the allottee of the suit plot nor was in possession thereof. The agreement, even if, entered into by him with defendant No.1 was not executable. After the death of plaintiffs' father. Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157. Bara Moghbazar they became the owners of the suit plot and they were in possession thereof Defendant No.1 entered into a contract with fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur without permission of RAJUK and claimed possession in the suit plot and thus posed threat to the plaintiffs' possession therein as well as their title. So the suit was maintainable. Defendant No.1 in his written statement admitted that the plaintiffs' father was the owner of the suit plot and thus, admitted the plaint case. The trial Court came to the further findings that the RS record of the suit plot was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs' predecessor. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza wherein his address had beenc cearly mentioned as 157. Bara Moghbazar which fact also confirmed that he was the allottee of the suit plot. The High Court Division, being the last Court of fact besides affirming the above findings of the trial Court, came to the finding that from 1967 till the hearing of the suit, i.e. more than 35 years, the plaintiffs had been in possession of the suit plot continuously and uninterruptedly and such possession gave them title and RAJUK, lessor always recognized the plaintiffs as lessees. In coming to the said finding, the High Court Division considered the documents filed by the plaintiffs, being 38 in number and the oral evidence as well. The High Court Division found the documents of the plaintiffs genuine. The High Court Division further held that defendant No.3 (plaintiff of Title Suit No.176 of 2004) claimed that he was in possession in the suit plot, but "no where he ever stated how he was inducted into possession and when he was dispossessed." The High Court Division further observed that had it been true that defendant No.3 sent his brother-in-law and the only son to the suit plot in 1972 and from there. both of them disappeared. then the defendant and the other family members would have left no stone untumed to find out their whereabouts but nothing was done. Although PWl Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (examined in Title Suit No.176 of 2004) stated that he made a GD entry over the incident. but copy of the GD entry was not produced. The High Court Division further observed that since the time of missing of the only son and the brother-in- law of plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. till the hearing of the appeals. he did not take any step either to recover the possession of the suit plot or for declaration that he was the lawful owner of the suit plot. The High Court Division further found that though the letter of allotment dated 21-3-1962. receipts showing deposit of installments against the suit plot. letter as to the delivery of possession of the suit plot approved plan by RAJUK for construction on the suit plot and the certified copy of the RS khatian Cexhibits- 1. 2 series. 3. 6 and 9 respectively) produced by defendant No.3 resemble or appear to be true are not genuine or true but he managed to get those documents which apparently appear to be original documents just to claim the suit property. In this appeal, the High Court Division also considered the fact that though plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (of Title Suit No.176 of 2004) claimed to have filed application before the Parliamentary Standing Committee, such application was neither exhibited nor filed and that "the file which according to him was opened was not called for." The High Court Division further observed that though defendant No.3 claimed that he entered into an agreement with MNH Bulu to sell the suit plot for which he applied to RAJUK for sale permission, but Bulu was not examined. The High Court Division further found that the plaintiffs' father, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, was the lessee of RAJUK and till his death, he exercised his right, title and interest over the suit plot to the knowledge of all. Exhibit-14 dated 7-4-1962 showed that possession of the suit plot was handed over to the father of the plaintiffs. The High Court Division separately considered exhibit-12 series, the original allotment letter and original copies of receipts of the payments of installments by the plaintiffs' father to the DIT against the suit plot; exhibit-17 , the loan sanction letter by the Housing Building Finance Corporation and exhbiit-17Ka dated 17-5-1967, the mortgage deed by which the suit plot was mortgaged by the plaintiffs' father with the House Building Finance Corporation in order to obtain loan; exhibits-18, 19, and 20 series which are the tenancy agreements, the gas bills, electricity bills and City Corporation tax receipts and rent receipts respectively and came to the further finding that it was proved "beyond any doubt" that the plaintiffs' father after getting lease of the suit plot from RAJUK had been exercising his continuous and uninterrupted possession therein. The High Court Division further considered exhibits-25 and 26 which proved that the suit plot was converted into a commercial plot from residential one at the instance of the plaintiffs' father, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar; exhibits-27 and 28 which proved that RAJUK accepted the transfer fees for converting the suit plot as a commercial plot and exhibit-29 showed the approval of plan of multi- storied commercial building by Eastern Housing Limited as the attorney of the plaintiffs' father and these documents showed that RAJUK accepted the plaintiffs' father, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as its lessee and did not accept Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur and the living Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (defendant No.3) as the lessee of the suit plot. The High Court Division came to the further finding that other two Shamsul Kabir Humayun Rezas who claimed the suit plot admittedly were not in possession thereof and both of them made agreement for sale of the suit plot "not as admitted lessee of RAJUK because their papers and documents filed in Title Suit No.51 of 2004 and 176 of 2004 never produced before RANK and claimed that they are the allottee of RAJUK." Plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was a fake person. These are all findings of facts. 

 54. This suit being a suit for title along with other prayers, we have also perused the evidence on record and found that the findings, given by the High Court Division in concurring with those of the trial Court, based on proper consideration of the evidence on record. The documents filed by the plaintiffs in support of their case that at the time of allottment of the suit plot by the then DIT, their father was the Executive Engineer of the then C&B and that he used to live at 157, Bara Moghbazar and got possession of the suit plot, paid the installments against the suit plot to the then PIT, got the standard lease deed, constructed building on the suit plot by taking 10 a.m. from the House Building Finance Corporation and had been in possession thereof althrough by letting out the same to the various tenants and now they are in possession thereof through their attorney, Eastern Housing Limited, are so interlinked and clockwise that no prudent man can have any difficulty to come to the decision as to the truth of their claim of title and possession in the suit plot. And a single broad fact as admitted by defendant No.3, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in his deposition as PW1 in Title Suit No. 176 of2004 (in this suit, hl1 was plaintiff and has evidence was adopted in Title Suit No.81 of 2006) that he did not go to the suit plot after December, 1972 when his only son and the brother-in-law disappeared, is enough to disbelieve his case that he was the actual allottee of the suit plot and also to conclude that he was trying to be an imposter just to claim the suit plot. In this regard, we are tempted to say that "possession follows title" and the very fact that the plaintiffs filed all the documents of possession, such as: RS Khatian prepared in the name of their father showing his address at 157, Bara Moghbazar, rent receipts, municipal tax receipts, bills of various utility services, the tenancy agreements first one being of the year, 1967, prima-facie, proved their possession in the suit plot, besides other documents already discussed earlier and the oral evidence: It is also necessary to state that defendant No.3 has failed to file any municipal tax receipts and utility services bills in respect of the suit plot to show that he ever asserted his title to the suit plot and possession therein. The trial Court rightly decreed the suit and the High Court Division committed no wrong in affirming the same.
